measurements.note: Two observations for the pinned headline; single observations otherwise; no p95.

comparison_baseline.custom_circuit_NPMULT03: 250,126 B packet / 3.08 s warm (4 threads) / 1.48 s serial verify / 13.3 GB RSS / AND 4,191,241 / witness log 23
comparison_baseline.witness_fixture: ~410 KB receipt data + few KB account/trie witness

capability_gaps_found.mulhu_missing: u128 arithmetic in the guest lowers to MULHU which upstream Jolt's expander does not dispatch (fail-closed UnsupportedInstruction); the guest uses u64-limb arithmetic instead — a real zkVM capability gap for 128-bit financial arithmetic, worked around here
capability_gaps_found.inline_registration_link: the host crate must depend on jolt-inlines-sha2 with the host feature or inline lookups fail with UnsupportedInstruction (inventory-based registration)
capability_gaps_found.guest_stack_limit: large stack arrays overflow the 4K-word guest stack silently corrupting memory (observed as garbage reads); heap allocation via extern crate alloc required

phase4_fold.pcs: DoryScheme (BN254) — NON-PQ, confirmed from jolt-sdk/src/host_utils.rs (VerifierPCS = DoryScheme; prove path = jolt_prover::dory::prove) and from the runtime loading ~/.cache/dory/dory_36.urs. The only PQ zkVM numbers in this lane remain JOLT_SCREEN's sha2-chain scales 18/20.

what_works.step1_k2: two near-chunk proofs proven and outer-verified (198.720 s / 155.917 s under load LA ~4.5-14 — NOT comparable to the pinned Phase 3 numbers 102.3 s), serialized fold input 3,011,037 B (verifier preprocessing + 2 proofs + 2 devices), postcard-framed 3,011,041 B
what_works.step1_k1: one near-chunk proof (211.608 s under load), fold input 2,912,738 B, framed 2,912,742 B
what_works.recursion_guest_build: std-mode RISC-V build works after adding rust-src to the pinned 1.95 toolchain; macro/host MemoryConfig alignment enforced by generating provable_macro.rs from rec_memory in the driver

what_failed.trace_step: the in-guest verification of ONE or TWO 98,154 B near-chunk proofs did not complete in any attempt (k=1 and k=2): 40-60+ minute traces, killed externally by the host environment's process-lifetime limit before producing the TRACE row count
what_failed.dory_setup_scale: the recursion preprocessing loads max_log_n=36 — the fold trace is ~2^36 rows, consistent with in-guest Dory verification of an 8.46M-cycle chunk proof being ~10^10-10^11 guest cycles
what_failed.environment: background processes are killed ~40-60 min after spawn (verified with a canary loop and four fold attempts); the trace phase cannot be checkpointed by the SDK's trace() API
what_failed.not_a_code_bug: step-1 serialization and all inner-proof outer-verifications pass; the stock fibonacci recursion reached Dory preprocessing in the same tree; the failure is trace-phase DURATION, exceeding the environment's process-lifetime window

fold_cost_model_from_measurements.inner_prove_class: ~102 s per chunk proof at pinned 4 threads (Phase 3 pinned numbers; this session's 156-212 s runs were load-affected)
fold_cost_model_from_measurements.fold_input_bytes: k=1: 2,912,742 B; k=2: 3,011,041 B (marginal ~98 KB per additional proof; the 2.8 MB fixed part is verifier preprocessing)
fold_cost_model_from_measurements.in_guest_verify_estimate: Dory setup max_log_n=36 => the fold statement is 2^36-scale; at the measured guest rate (8.46M rows for the chunk workload; the recursion guest's verification arithmetic is 100-1000x the deserialization) the in-guest verify of one chunk proof is plausibly 10^10-10^11 cycles => trace tens of minutes to hours => fold prove on the order of hours on this CPU. THIS IS AN ESTIMATE, labeled as such; the trace step is what would measure it exactly and it does not fit this environment.
fold_cost_model_from_measurements.aggregation_verdict: zkVM recursive folding of near-chunk-sized proofs is CPU-intractable at this workload scale: the fold costs more than re-verifying the proofs directly (host verify 0.133 s each).

bugs_found_and_fixed: inventory inline registrations dead-stripped by --gc-sections: the guest crate must be a host dependency for its registration tables to survive (fold driver now depends on near-chunk-guest)
missing rust-src on the pinned 1.95 toolchain blocked the recursion guest's std-mode build
macro/host MemoryConfig must match exactly or the emulator MMU faults (driver now generates provable_macro.rs from its rec_memory)
the recursion guest's verify(bytes) needs postcard framing of the record buffer as a single slice
the stock recursion example REGENERATES provable_macro.rs on every run — fold drivers must own the macro file or they build with whatever the last stock run left behind
